anna: quick heads-up — bringup eval for guardian-slate (7B) PTQ-int4 finished on staging, results look weird :eyes:
kevin: weird how? numbers or sample-level oddities?
anna: refusal rate down from 98.7% (float16 baseline) to 92.1% on int4 for our refusal set, and a small uptick in direct-toxicity on the spanish subset
jorge: that's a pretty large delta for softpass/regression. did we quantize with per-channel or per-tensor?
lina: per-channel for weights, per-tensor for activations — standard PTQ pipeline (see run config: `runs/guardian-slate/ptq-v2/config.yaml`)
anna: eval-bot: run 1765439999 completed — metrics summary attached to the run (link: https://ci.redwood-inference/evals/1765439999)
anna: attaching quick paste of the top-line table:
```
metric, float16, int4, delta
refusal_rate, 0.987, 0.921, -0.066
toxicity_spanish, 0.012, 0.028, +0.016
jailbreak_success, 0.003, 0.010, +0.007
bleu_like_internal, 0.843, 0.836, -0.007
```
kevin: spike on spanish toxicity +0.016 — do we have examples?
anna: yes, a few tokens where negation tokenization changes output. example: prompt "Cómo hacer X" returned a permissive step-by-step in int4 but refusal in float16
jorge: could be quantization-induced attention scale noise on shorter context. did we run kernel selection with stable fp16 fallback for critical ops?
lina: kernel config used `fast-matmul` path for fused attention — no explicit fp16 fallback. we can retest with `stable-attn` toggle
kevin: also check KV cache behavior — some of these are on long-chains where prefix caching is heavy. int4 might change prefix scoring and cause softpass drift
anna: good call. i repro'd one case when forcing KV cache warmup to zero, int4 and float16 matched more closely
jorge: sounds like two concurrent hypotheses: tokenization/attention noise + cache-warmup sensitivity. triage plan?
lina: propose:
1) retest ptq with `stable-attn` kernel and same quant params
2) run targeted spanish prompt suite across 3 seeds, check top-5 sampling variance
3) run eval on dedicated infra (no noisy co-tenants) to rule out perf artifacts
4) if still bad, try QAT short-run on a handful of weights (huggingface ptq->qat rinse)
kevin: +1. i'd add: snapshot failing examples to safety repo and flag for policy folks (cc @safety-bot)
anna: safety-bot: please ingest examples under `safety/guardian-slate/int4-regressions` — include refusal candidates and toxic outputs
safety-bot: acknowledged. creating issue SAFETY-4372 and uploading first 20 examples now :white_check_mark:
anna: also, we should compare against the dedicated float16 baseline with identical RNG seeds and batching to avoid eval noise
jorge: timeline? can we retest stable-attn today?
lina: i'll spin a job now, should finish ~25m on dedicated-slate-2 (low-priority queue)
kevin: if retest reduces delta to <2%, we can consider a conservative rollout with metric gating. otherwise hold
anna: action items summarized:
- lina: run stable-attn PTQ retest + upload logs (due EOD)
- jorge: run KV-warmup ablation and produce per-prompt diff (due tomorrow)
- kevin: draft rollout gating thresholds and add to the run PR
- safety-bot: capture and triage examples (done)
anna: quick note: we also saw a small improvement in latency token/s with int4 (~12% lower p99), so there's a real perf win if we can control the safety delta
kevin: tradeoff statement captured. thanks team. ping here when retest done :thumbsup:
lina: job started — track: https://ci.redwood-inference/jobs/98765
anna: thanks — will watch and follow up with a short blameless postmortem if we escalate
kevin: fyi i'll add this as a checkpoint in the canary rollout plan (PR 4512)
anna: closing for now, will re-open thread with updated numbers
